pr_title: coredump: allow only empty messages after first "sentinel"
pr_comments:
@poettering PTAL.

Btw, not sure if we helped code readability now, I feel like not really

This should not carry "Fixes #34130" because this only one facet of that bug, but not the other issue.

Just do "See #34130".

> This should not carry "Fixes #34130" because this only one facet of that bug, but not the other issue.
> 
> Just do "See #34130".

And, as explained in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/34944#issuecomment-2447768168 with that edit it means it has now disappeared from the tracking and linking both here:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b14aff3-1341-438d-8aa5-910f81d562f2)

and on the issue:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6365020-2010-4866-af51-ca0b19dbb11a)

So I've put it back in the PR description so that they are properly linked so I can track it, please leave it there.

With the fixes, the linking and tracking works both here:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90f30e75-2596-4e6a-a655-6472dcd028e7)

and on the issue:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd3a1316-ee9a-441e-afb1-6cd86c6285ef)

sorry, but let's *not* do this nonsensical close-reopen-close-reopen-close-reopen business. It's idiotic. It's entirely sufficient if there's a message in the issue at the bottom if one of many issues has been addressed. 

It's the last fix that should close the issue, not the first. I am not sure in which universe closing it on the first would ever make sense.

> It's entirely sufficient if there's a message in the issue at the bottom if one of many issues has been addressed.

No, it is not sufficient, as anything and anybody can drop a comment mentioning one issue from another, for any reason, even across repositories and organisations, so it is NOT a reliable way of tracking.

The reliable way of tracking is the aforementioned sidebar menu. I agree that it sucks that it's the only way to use it right now, but I can't change that, only Github can.

> let's not do this nonsensical close-reopen-close-reopen-close-reopen business. It's idiotic

Agreed. systemd commit messages "fixing" things without actually fully fixing them don't make much sense. That being said it has been happening for a while (and it doesn't affect the "fixes" thing only) so personally I just ignore whatever is written there most of the time. One option would probably be to open a bunch of different issues (instead of one "umbrella" issue) to let commits saying that they fix them close them. (I can't say it makes much sense either though)
